extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki contributors and editors (especially new users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and house-style rules for contributing content, proofs, and edits to ProofWiki (how to write, edit, refactor, and format pages). Targeted at users who create or maintain ProofWiki pages and talk-page posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not replace existing proofs; add additional proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not you like a particular proof is irrelevant; multiple proofs are allowed for any given theorem. Rather than replace an existing proof with your own, add your new proof as an additional proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put each separate proof into its own subpage which is then transcluded into the main page (example: 'Real Numbers are Uncountable'). Deleting others' material is considered rude; if you object to content, raise it on the associated talk page as the author may have made a mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \left and \right for every pair of parentheses (house LaTeX rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforce the use of \left(...\right) pairs for parentheses so that braces are properly paired and parentheses size appropriately to their content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curly braces group tokens for TeX and help editors find matching braces; this avoids problems with copy-pasting and later edits that change vertical size. Equation references like (1) and (3′) are exceptions. NOTE: this rule has been largely superseded by ProofWiki-specific LaTeX commands (see Symbols:LaTeX Commands/ProofWiki Specific).

rubrics_metrics.name: One sentence per line
rubrics_metrics.description: House style requires placing a single sentence on each line to break the flow of argument into well-defined steps, making proofs easier to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is strictly enforced; unlike printed textbooks (which save space), the website spreads out arguments for clarity. Expect edits that break long paragraphs into sentence-per-line form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert extra blank lines between sections (two blank lines at section end)
rubrics_metrics.description: The house style spreads sections out: insert two blank lines at the end of every section before the next (sub)header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a deliberate presentation decision to improve readability. Editing only an individual section is discouraged because MediaWiki removes extra blank lines when editing a section; you may need to edit the whole page to restore them. There are a few specialised exceptions where breaking the rule improves presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve redirects unless it is safe to delete them
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep redirects from old or less-meaningful page titles to avoid breaking internal and external links; only delete a redirect after every page that links to it has been updated to the new target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'What links here' to find pages linking to a redirect. Even if internal links are fixed, external websites may still link to the old title; deleting the redirect removes that external link (undesirable). For very new pages (e.g., small typo in title), it is usual to delete the redirect after renaming. Note: more recently the site has taken to deleting redirects as soon as linking pages are updated, so practice has evolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign your posts on talk pages
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting on talk pages, you are required to sign your post so that there's a record of who said what and when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Signature and timestamp' button (or type --~~~~). On save, the four tildes are replaced by your user signature and the posting date. This applies to talk pages, not main content pages (definitions or proofs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and maintain 'Sources' section link flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sources' section attempts to provide a path through the site mirroring the reading experience of the cited source using 'previous' and 'next' links; you must not break that linear ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you change page names or copy pages, you must either: (a) remove the citation if the new page does not correspond to material in the source work, or (b) amend the links that define the source flow on the surrounding pages, or (c) invoke the {{SourceReview}} template in the 'Sources' section to alert maintainers. Failure to do so compromises the reading flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refactoring must produce standalone subpages and preserve sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Refactoring (splitting pages into subpages to be transcluded) is not merely extracting a section; the new page must be standalone and handle theorem statements, proofs, and source citations appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When refactoring, include the statement of the theorem on the new page and wrap the proof in 'onlyinclude' tags so only the proof is transcluded. Attend carefully to source reference sections to avoid compromising linear source flow. Blindly copying link sections into the new page is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refactoring is for experienced editors familiar with ProofWiki
rubrics_metrics.description: Refactoring is considered a task best left to experienced editors — specifically those experienced in ProofWiki's philosophy and house style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New contributors should explore existing pages, learn how code is styled, and observe maintenance tags and edits made to their own contributions before attempting refactoring. If a user hasn't learned or accepted the house style, they are requested not to embark on refactoring tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep pages small and use transclusion for large content
rubrics_metrics.description: The site policy is to keep pages small (few pages over ten thousand characters) and to split large pages into transcluded subpages where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large pages are candidates for refactoring; this helps maintain readability and manageability. Refactoring must still respect standalone-ness and sources (see refactoring entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain high level of rigor in cross-linking and consistent style
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond merely posting mathematics, contributors should aim for consistent style and a high level of rigor especially in the context of cross-linking between pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the site's philosophy that distinguishes ProofWiki from other wikis; contributors are expected to learn by example and accept stylistic conventions. Expect maintainers to adjust submissions to match house standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates and maintenance tags appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: When changes affect structure or source flow, use the appropriate maintenance templates (e.g., {{SourceReview}}) and tags to alert maintainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoking templates helps coordinate maintenance tasks rather than silently leaving pages in an inconsistent state after edits or copies.
